exampleAnswers.title: Computing a Probability at a Single Point

question.explanation:
If $X$ follows a discrete uniform distribution over a set $S,$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{|S|}, & x \in S \\[5pt] 0, &\textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Here, we have $X \sim U \left\lbrace 5, 6, 7, 8, 9,10\right\rbrace,$ and the set $S = \left\lbrace 5, 6, 7, 8, 9,10 \right\rbrace$ has $|S|=6$ items. So, we have

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{6}, & x = 5, 6, 7, 8, 9,10 \\[5pt] 0, &\textrm{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]

Therefore,

\[ P(X = 8) = f(8) = \dfrac{1}{6}. \]
